proposal.title: Prompt-release-ordered decode admission for online non-clairvoyant disaggregated serving: a revise-level proposal
proposal.hypothesis: In a slot-level two-pool simulator with online arrivals and unknown output lengths, ordering the decode-admission queue by retained prompt size (largest prompt first), instead of FIFO, under the same certified-lower-bound reservation and eviction rules, lowers total completion time by at least 5% without raising P99 completion time by more than 5%.
proposal.baseline: The simplest strong baseline is an online FIFO two-pool policy that applies the DMRS prefill memory constraint (sum over E and W of p_i, plus p_new, must not exceed M_P). Decode admission is FIFO and reserves p_i+õ_i, where õ_i is the certified lower bound. Overflow is resolved with Chen A_min ordered eviction (2508.14544v2 Algorithm 2). No executable code is supplied for DMRS, A_min, the Feng GSA/Response algorithms or Arrow. That is a baseline-coverage gap: every baseline must be reimplemented in simulation from the pseudocode.
proposal.operator_delta: Change only the scan order of the decode-admission waiting set W from FIFO to nonincreasing p_i, with ties broken by arrival time. Reservation, eviction and prefill admission stay identical.

contribution_claims.text: A minimal decode-admission ordering operator that targets release of retained prefill KV under non-clairvoyance.
An online two-pool simulator with a checked memory-safety invariant and a restart cost model that includes re-prefill.
Hypothesized change in TCT and P99 relative to FIFO/work-conserving/backpressure controls. This is a simulation-only hypothesis.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: Source-supported: DMRS uses known d_i, a batch released at t=0, instantaneous transfer and non-preemptive phases. Chen A_min uses a single pool, identical prompts and cancellation. Feng uses a single pool with kill-and-restart. The target setting has online arrivals, unknown d_i and two pools, and it permits decode eviction. Those source regimes are excluded from the target, not contradicted by it. No source guarantee transfers to the target.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: Each slot t runs these steps. (1) Remove finished decode requests; the end-of-sequence event is the only signal of d_i. (2) Move requests that finished prefill (S^P+m_i=t) to W. (3) Overflow check: if the sum over D of (p_j+a_j+1) exceeds M_D, evict in increasing order of õ_j. Each evicted job sets õ_j=a_j, discards its KV and re-enters U, so it must prefill again. (4) Scan W in the chosen order and admit i if the sum over D of (p_j+max(a_j+1,õ_j)), plus p_i+õ_i, does not exceed M_D. Admission transfers the KV and frees p_i from prefill memory. (5) Scan U in FIFO order and admit to prefill if the sum over E∪W of p, plus p_i, does not exceed M_P. Invariant: neither pool constraint is violated in any slot, because step 3 runs before any decode growth. A request that runs past õ_i triggers the overflow check rather than violating memory. Inputs are only p_i, m_i, arrival times and observed tokens a_j. No true lengths are used.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: At first admission õ_i equals ℓ for all requests, so the new order reduces to largest-prompt-first. Its effect is to free more prefill memory per admission while spending more decode memory per admission. Whether the net effect is positive is not derivable from the sources and is unresolved. It could equally hurt by starving short-prompt requests in W and raising P99.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: FIFO decode admission, or smallest-reservation-first ordering by p_i+õ_i as in A_min batch formation. Both have equal O(|W| log|W|) cost per slot. The smallest-first variant maximizes decode concurrency but frees less prefill memory.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Sweep the ratio M_P/M_D on small synthetic traces. The operator should help only where prefill memory is binding. If gains do not grow as M_P shrinks, the claimed coupling mechanism is absent.

data_paths.possible_leakage: Trace generators that sort by output length or correlate arrival order with d_i. Audit that d_i is read only by the EOS oracle.

proposal.counterexample: All prompts are equal. The order then reduces to FIFO, so no effect is possible. Separately, when long-prompt requests also have long outputs, decode memory saturates, evictions rise and P99 worsens.
proposal.matched_control: The identical policy with FIFO decode ordering, using the same reservation, eviction, prefill admission, capacities, information and seeds. Additional controls: work-conserving FIFO without reservation, and a backpressure policy that blocks prefill admission when W exceeds a threshold.

experiment.development: Fresh synthetic Poisson and bursty arrivals with lognormal prompt and output lengths. Use 20 seeds and a sweep over M_P/M_D, run in a local CPU simulator.
experiment.heldout: A new generator family (Pareto outputs, prompt-output correlation ρ in {-0.5, 0.5}) with seeds drawn after development is frozen. No reuse of DMRS or Arrow fixtures.
experiment.metric: Total completion time and P99 completion time, each as a ratio to the FIFO control. Report the median across seeds with bootstrap 95% CI. Also report eviction count.
experiment.kill_threshold: Reject if the TCT ratio CI upper bound exceeds 0.97 on held-out, or if the median P99 ratio exceeds 1.05.

proposal.prior_art_difference: Overlap: the two-pool constraints come from DMRS, eviction from A_min and restart cost from Feng; Arrow does adaptive instance flipping. The only proposed difference is the W ordering by retained prompt size. That difference is unverified and may be a trivial heuristic. Literature coverage is bounded, and no local experiment matches this proposal.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: Source assumptions: DMRS is offline, has known d_i, a batch released at t=0, non-preemptive phases and instantaneous transfer. A_min and Feng GSA use a single pool, and Feng GSA uses identical prompts. Response permits heterogeneous prompts but uses a single pool. Target assumptions: online arrivals, unknown d_i, two pools, and permitted decode eviction with re-prefill. These are excluded regimes, not contradictions, so no source guarantee transfers. A separate gap: the target needs an initial õ_i (ℓ), but no prediction source is specified. If ℓ=1, the reservation p_i+õ_i is essentially p_i, and admission is nearly work-conserving.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: At slot t: set W'=sort(W, key=-p_i, tie=arrival). For each i in W', admit i if Σ_{j∈D}(p_j+max(a_j+1,õ_j)) + p_i + õ_i ≤ M_D. On admission, release p_i from M_P. Next, admit from U in FIFO order while Σ_{E∪W} p + p_i ≤ M_P. The only operation changed relative to the FIFO control is the permutation of W. Because the scan greedily skips infeasible requests, the permutation changes which subset is admitted. Under largest-first, a large p_i that fails the decode check is skipped and smaller requests may still enter, so the ordering is not strictly blocking.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: The permutation is not a no-op when prompts differ. It trades prefill memory freed per admission (Δ_P=+p_i) against decode memory consumed per admission (p_i+õ_i). The net effect on total completion time depends on which pool binds. It also interacts with eviction: larger admitted p_j makes overflow eviction costlier, since an evicted job re-prefills p_j in M_P. The sign of the effect is unresolved. A plausible failure mode is that largest-first lowers decode concurrency, so it lengthens per-request waiting in W for small requests and raises P99.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: Two orderings at identical O(|W|log|W|) cost per slot. (a) FIFO. (b) Smallest-first by p_i+õ_i or by m_i, the non-clairvoyant analogue of DMRS's m_i+d_i key and A_min's ascending õ_i. Smallest-first maximizes the number of admitted requests, which is the standard sum-of-completion-times heuristic, but frees less prefill memory. A backpressure control that blocks prefill admission when W is large directly targets the same coupling without reordering.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Run a two-request analytic toy and a small-trace sweep over M_P/M_D, with ρ(p,d) fixed at 0 and the three orderings (FIFO, smallest-first, largest-first) under identical seeds. Largest-first must beat smallest-first, not just FIFO, in the regime where M_P binds. If smallest-first matches or dominates it everywhere, the ordering contribution does not survive.

review.reason: The mechanism is coherent and nonredundant at the level of a permutation: greedy skipping makes admitted sets order-dependent. However, the matched controls omit the most obvious competitor, smallest-first ordering, which is the non-clairvoyant reduction of the DMRS and A_min keys. Beating FIFO alone would not isolate the claimed release-of-prefill-memory mechanism. The initial õ_i is also unspecified, which changes the reservation semantics.

review.strongest_counterargument: When M_P is the bottleneck, prefill admission stalls behind W. Freeing the largest p_i then unlocks the most U admissions per decode admission, which smallest-first cannot do. The effect could therefore be real in that regime, even if it is regime-specific.
review.required_test: Add smallest-first (by p_i+õ_i and by m_i) and backpressure as matched controls, and specify initial õ_i. Sweep M_P/M_D at ρ=0 and ρ=±0.5. Accept only if largest-first beats the best of these controls on held-out total completion time with P99 ratio ≤1.05 where M_P binds.
